item.title: Fixing Bash Shell Expansion Issues When Echoing '#!' String
item.description:
“Fixing Bash Shell Expansion Issues When Echoing ‘#!’ String”

When executing commands in a Bash shell, particularly when attempting to print the shebang sequence #! using the echo command within double quotes, users often encounter issues stemming from csh-style history expansion. This mechanism treats the exclamation mark (!) specially, leading to unexpected command execution or errors like "event not found".

How can one reliably output the literal string #! in Bash, circumventing this history expansion feature?

item.title: Bash Shell Quoting: Literal vs. Expanded Values Explained
item.description:
“Bash Shell Quoting: Literal vs. Expanded Values Explained”

When working with the bash shell, precisely controlling how your strings are interpreted is crucial for writing reliable and secure scripts. This involves understanding the distinct behaviors of single quotes (') and double quotes (") and how they interact with variables and special characters.

The Power of Literal Interpretation with Single Quotes

Single quotes offer the most straightforward way to ensure that a string is treated exactly as it appears. Anything enclosed within single quotes is preserved literally, meaning no character is interpreted specially by the shell.
